content.overview: Section 18 of the Registration Act, 1908 lists documents of which registration is optional. They include instruments other than wills affecting immovable property of a value less than one hundred rupees; acknowledgements of consideration for such instruments; leases of immovable property for a term not exceeding one year, and leases exempted under section 17; instruments assigning a decree or order affecting immovable property below that value; instruments affecting movable property; wills; and other documents not required by section 17 to be registered. Optional means the Act does not compel registration. It does not mean an unregistered document in the section 17 list is valid.
content.study: Use section 18 only after section 17 does not apply. A will is the clearest optional document. A lease not exceeding one year, with no yearly rent, is optional. An instrument that section 17 catches cannot be saved by calling it optional.

learningObjectives: State that section 18 permits but does not compel registration.
Place wills, movable-property instruments and sub-Rs 100 immovable instruments in the optional list.
Keep section 17 documents out of section 18.
enhancement.definition: Section 18 is the optional-registration list. Registration is allowed, and not required, for the documents named in it.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Optional registration is the residual class. Compulsory registration under section 17 prevails where both descriptions might seem to fit.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Registration Act, 1908, sections 18 and 17. Section 49 does not apply to a document that section 17 does not require to be registered, unless another Act requires registration.
essentialIngredients: Lease not exceeding one year and not otherwise compulsory
Or another document not required by section 17
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 18 is permissive. The parties may register for preservation and notice, but the Act does not invalidate the document merely because they do not. The value band below one hundred rupees is the mirror of the section 17 band. A lease for a term not exceeding one year is optional unless it reserves a yearly rent or otherwise falls into section 17. Instruments of movable property, including shares in movable form, are optional under this section. A will is expressly optional. Registration of a will, if chosen, has its own deposit and presentation rules later in the Act; those rules are not the compulsory list. If the document in fact creates or extinguishes a right of one hundred rupees or more in immovable property, section 17 applies and section 18 cannot be pleaded.
examples: A will of a house is not registered. Section 18 permits that choice.
An eight-month lease with no yearly rent is left unregistered. Section 18 covers it.
A sale deed of land worth more than Rs 100 is called optional. Section 17, not section 18, applies.
enhancement.problemApplication: Check section 17 first. Only if the document is outside it, and outside any Transfer of Property Act registration requirement, treat registration as optional.
distinctions: Lease not exceeding one year vs a lease exceeding one year
Movable-property instrument vs immovable instrument of Rs 100 or more
